memory: I've learned to be more mindful of my health as I've gotten older. It's amazing how much of a difference small lifestyle changes can make. And living in Kansas with its unpredictable weather means I have to be flexible with my routine. Some days I can get outside and enjoy a long walk, but other times I'm stuck inside due to the cold winters or severe storms. Despite the challenges, I try to stay active, eat well, and manage my stress levels. It's all about finding that balance.I've made significant changes to my diet since being diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes. I've learned to be mindful of my carb intake and have replaced pasta and bread with healthier options like whole grains, lean proteins, and plenty of vegetables. It was tough at first, but now it's just second nature. My go-to breakfast is Greek yogurt with nuts and berries or eggs with avocado. For lunch, I keep it simple with grilled chicken and a salad. And for dinner, I love making soups, especially during the winter. There's nothing better than a warm bowl of homemade vegetable soup on a freezing day!I've come to realize that consistency is more important than intensity when it comes to exercise. I used to think I needed to run miles or lift heavy weights, but I've found that walking has been my best friend. It's low impact, which is great for my osteoarthritis, and it helps with my blood sugar levels. I also try to do some light yoga a few times a week. I never thought I'd be someone who did yoga, but it actually helps a lot with my joint pain and flexibility. On days when the weather's bad, I use a stationary bike or do some at-home workouts. Nothing fancy, just enough to keep me moving.I've learned to prioritize sleep as I've gotten older. It's amazing how crucial it is for my overall health. If I don't get a good night's rest, my blood pressure spikes, my joints ache, and my energy is gone. I used to stay up late watching TV, but now I have a bedtime routine that helps me wind down. I avoid caffeine after 3 PM, keep my bedroom cool and dark, and read a book before bed instead of looking at my phone. It's made a huge difference.I've found that stress management has been a game-changer for me. Stress is a huge trigger for my hypertension, and when life gets busy, I can feel it physically. To combat this, I've started practicing mindfulness—just five minutes of deep breathing or meditation in the morning. It sounded silly to me at first, but it actually works. I've also started keeping a gratitude journal where I jot down three good things that happened each day. It helps me stay positive, even on tough days.I've made a conscious effort to stay hydrated as I've gotten older. It's amazing how much of a difference it makes for my energy levels, digestion, and even my skin. I keep a big water bottle with me all day and try to drink herbal teas in the evening instead of coffee. Kansas summers can be brutal, so I make sure to drink even more water when it's hot outside.I make sure to stay on top of preventative care by getting regular check-ups, taking my medications on time, and getting vaccinated every year. I also prioritize annual screenings like my mammogram and bone density tests, as osteoporosis runs in my family. By catching potential issues early, I can prevent them from becoming bigger problems.I've learned to be kind to myself on days when I don't feel like working out or cooking a healthy meal. It's not about being perfect; it's about being consistent. I try to make better choices the next day and remind myself that it's okay to have off days.I'm feeling pretty good about where I am right now. I know I can't control everything about my health, but I do what I can to stay strong and feel my best. If I've learned anything over the years, it's that small habits add up. It's not about making drastic changes; it's about making choices every day that support my well-being. I'm in it for the long haul!
